BiblicalUsage: Bildad uses this word for the spark of the wicked man's fire, a flame split into tongues that is about to go out. The light of the wicked shall be put out, he says, and the spark shall not shine.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a flame built on wickedness has no staying power, and Bildad's picture of the dying spark is exactly right about where it ends.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
